title: Derived completeness of a complex of modules
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring and let $D(A)$ be the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of the abelian category of $A$-modules. Let $K\in D(A)$ and $f\in A$. Write $T(K,f)$ for a derived limit [def-weil-derived-limit] in $D(A)$ of the inverse system

$$
 \cdots\xrightarrow{\ f\ }K\xrightarrow{\ f\ }K\xrightarrow{\ f\ }K,
$$

every term of which is $K$ and every transition map of which is multiplication by $f$. For an ideal $I\subset A$, the object $K$ is *derived complete with respect to $I$* if, for every $f\in I$, every such derived limit $T(K,f)$ is zero. An $A$-module $M$ is derived complete with respect to $I$ if $M[0]\in D(A)$ is. (This is a condition on objects of $D(A)$ itself, as opposed to the coefficient-sheaf form on a pro-etale site in [def-weil-derived-complete].)

mathlib_searches.query: Derived completeness of a complex of modules with respect to an ideal defined by vanishing of the derived inverse limit of multiplication by each element of the ideal

An object K of the derived category of modules over a commutative ring is derived complete for an ideal I when the homotopy limit of the constant tower with transition multiplication by f vanishes for every f in I
